lines.text: One day in 1972, every car in Nigeria switched sides of the road.
Under British rule, Nigerians drove on the left, like in the UK.
But Nigeria's neighbours, Benin, Niger, Chad and Cameroon, all drive on the right.
So on April second, 1972, Nigeria changed over to driving on the right.
Ghana made the same switch two years later, in 1974.
And in 1973, Nigeria swapped the pound for a brand new currency: the naira.
